sources.title: Greater Monrovia Urban Review: A Spatial Analysis Investigating Constraints and Opportunities
sources.temporal_coverage: Spatial and service data mainly from 2008–2020; report version 2020.
sources.methodology: Spatial analysis of informal land use, urban services, household data and flood hazards using GIS and community mapping.
sources.limitations: Baseline data are mostly from 2008–2019; Greater Monrovia findings are not nationally representative.

sources.title: FAO GIEWS Country Brief on Liberia
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Global Information and Early Warning System
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 rainy season and harvest; food-security estimate October–December 2025; forecast June–August 2026.
sources.methodology: FAO country brief using cereal-balance, satellite crop-monitoring and food-security data.
sources.limitations: This brief predates later season-specific verification.

sources.title: Peacebuilding, Reconciliation, and Social Cohesion Project
geographic_coverage: Tewor District, Grand Cape Mount County
sources.temporal_coverage: Project period 15 January 2020–31 December 2024; listed local achievements through 2023.
sources.methodology: Official UNDP project summary and reported activities and achievements.
sources.limitations: Project webpage is not an independent evaluation; achievements are reported by the implementer.

sources.title: USD 103.9M SARTLA Project Launched to Strengthen Liberia’s Climate Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: SARTLA project period 2025–2030; launch reported May 2026.
sources.methodology: UNDP launch release describing project scope and reproducing government and partner statements.
sources.limitations: County risk descriptions are official remarks, not a measured local hazard survey; project aims are not outcomes.

sources.title: Environmental and Social Impact Assessment for the Monrovia Metropolitan Climate Resilience Project
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Liberia; Environmental Protection Agency of Liberia
geographic_coverage: West Point community, Monrovia Metropolitan Area
sources.temporal_coverage: Project assessment page published March 2026; project phases not dated in the page excerpt.
sources.methodology: UNDP publication-page summary of a project environmental and social risk assessment and management plan.
sources.limitations: The linked 33 MB ESIA PDF exceeded the reader limit; claims are restricted to the official page summary.

claims.paraphrase: Duala Market in New Kru Town has fragmented, blocked storm drains with no coherent outflow; local discussions report common peak-rainy-season flooding. Wetland-adjacent toilets also pose groundwater-contamination risks.
claims.limitations: Market findings are from the 2020 assessment, not a current flood-event count.

claims.locator: Printed pp.65–67, municipal governance and service delivery
claims.paraphrase: The review says years of conflict left Greater Monrovia's political and administrative authority centrally controlled, limiting fiscal allocation and local governments' ability to provide adequate services.
claims.limitations: General post-conflict governance finding; the review does not evaluate climate-adaptation delivery.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It explicitly attributes centralization to years of conflict and links it to constrained local resources and services.

claims.locator: FAO GIEWS brief, 9 January 2026, 2025 crop and rainfall findings
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports 2025 dry spells after near- or below-average rainfall in May–August, followed by localized flood-related crop losses in Grand Bassa, Margibi, Montserrado and Sinoe counties.
claims.limitations: Weather observations are not attributed to anthropogenic climate change.

claims.locator: FAO GIEWS brief, 9 January 2026, food-security estimate and forecast
claims.paraphrase: FAO estimated 418,000 people (7%) in Cadre Harmonisé Phase 3 during October–December 2025 and projected 506,000 (9%) for June–August 2026; surveyed household shocks included floods alongside illness, death, job loss and prices.
claims.scenario: Cadre Harmonisé estimate and forecast; no climate-emissions scenario.

claims.locator: FAO GIEWS brief, 9 January 2026, 2025 government support
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports that in 2025 the government provided farmers cash for land preparation, inputs, mechanization and equipment; the brief says this support enabled area expansion and improved yields.
claims.limitations: No causal programme evaluation is supplied.

claims.locator: FAO GIEWS brief, 9 January 2026, Liberians Feed Yourselves Agenda
claims.paraphrase: The 2024–2030 Agenda targets 50,000 hectares of lowland irrigated rice development over five years in Lofa, Nimba and Bong counties.
claims.limitations: Target is planned, not completed or evaluated.

claims.paraphrase: UNDP lists land and boundary disputes, inter-group and political tensions, youth unemployment, natural-resource mismanagement, corruption, weak state trust and over-centralization as constraints to peace and social cohesion.
institutions: Independent National Commission on Human Rights
claims.limitations: UNDP project-page diagnosis; not a new climate-conflict study or independent causal evaluation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The page identifies land disputes and natural-resource governance problems as threats to sustained peace.

claims.locator: UNDP project page, reported achievements in Sanoyea District
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports that Palava Hut hearings in Sanoyea District, Bong County, heard 52 cases and amicably resolved all but one; the page reports 328 cases resolved during 2022.
claims.limitations: Implementer-reported historical results; the page does not evaluate durability or climate-program links.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNDP describes the hearings as supporting post-conflict healing, reconciliation and peaceful coexistence.

claims.locator: UNDP launch release, EPA remarks on county climate risks
claims.paraphrase: EPA remarks identify farmers in Bong and Lofa, coastal fishers in Grand Cape Mount and Montserrado, and communities in Maryland, Margibi and Nimba as facing rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, coastal erosion and environmental degradation.
claims.limitations: These are attributed government remarks, not a quantified county-level hazard assessment.

claims.locator: UNDP launch release, SARTLA project description
claims.paraphrase: The 2025–2030 SARTLA project aims to support climate-smart agriculture, sustainable fisheries, ecosystem restoration, coastal and land management, climate finance, and livelihoods across seven counties, with emphasis on women and youth.
claims.limitations: These are planned objectives of a recently launched project, not verified resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: UNDP ESIA publication page, report summary
claims.paraphrase: An EPA-implemented, UNDP-supervised and GCF-funded climate-resilience project targets vulnerable West Point, exposed to sea-level rise and intense storms; the ESIA page says the plan includes environmental and social safeguards.
claims.limitations: The linked ESIA was not read because its PDF exceeded the reader limit; only the official page summary is asserted.

search_audit.query: Liberia county-level 2025 rainfall variability, floods, crop losses and food-security estimates primary FAO sources
search_audit.outcome: Found FAO's January 2026 brief with county-level flood crop losses and a current-to-publication food-security outlook; World Bank spatial analysis adds named Greater Monrovia exposure sites.

search_audit.query: Liberia climate change, land/resource disputes, peacebuilding and local social cohesion primary UN evidence
search_audit.outcome: UNDP's project page identifies boundary/land disputes and natural-resource mismanagement as peace constraints and reports local mediation results; no source found attributing violence to climate shocks.

search_audit.query: Liberia civil conflict legacy, urban governance and climate-flood adaptation capacity in Greater Monrovia
search_audit.outcome: World Bank review explicitly links years of conflict to centralized authority and constrained local resources/services; it does not directly evaluate climate-adaptation programs or say insecurity blocks their delivery.

search_audit.query: Liberia current climate-resilience projects, county coverage, coastal safeguards, agricultural and peacebuilding capacities
search_audit.outcome: UNDP reports SARTLA's 2025–2030 plans and the West Point climate project safeguards; FAO reports 2025 agricultural support, and UNDP lists historical county-level Palava Hut mediation. Project aims are not outcomes.

gaps: No reviewed primary source directly attributes conflict or violence to climate shocks; the post-conflict governance finding is not evidence that climate adaptation is obstructed.
The UNDP ESIA PDF was too large for the reader; only its official publication-page summary is used.
The FAO food-security forecast for June–August 2026 was issued in January 2026; this extraction does not establish what was later realized.
The Greater Monrovia spatial review is a 2020 baseline and the UNDP Palava Hut results are historical implementer-reported achievements; neither should be treated as current 2026 outcome evidence.
SARTLA and West Point adaptation interventions are described as plans or safeguards; no reviewed source provides an independent outcome evaluation.
